candidates.title: Finding Blind Spots in AppWorld and WorkArena Task Verifiers
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026 workshop poster ("Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development")
candidates.citationVelocity: published 6 days (submitted 2026-10-06); Semantic Scholar API 429 rate-limited on every attempt, no data available
communitySignals: OpenReview supplement published (construction grammar, evidence, count reproducer)
credibilityEvidence: Table 2 (AppWorld fault-arm results): 6/15 constructed Extra-NI effects passed across 2/5 eligible generators
WorkArena prospective rerun: 23 pre-selected PASS cells, independent Table API readback confirmed nondefault values in 21/23
cardinality patch (len(added_*)==N) applied to checker copies flips all 6 AppWorld cells to Fail, confirming the mechanism
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Confirms specific constructed false-accept mechanisms in two benchmark families with small sample counts; author explicitly states these are fixed-census counts, not an independently sampled population-rate estimate
reproducibilityEvidence: OpenReview supplement with construction grammar, primary evidence, content-bound stage lineage, count reproducer
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Author's claim scope (confirmed mechanism, not population rate) matches exactly what the evidence supports
candidates.primaryLimitation: Confirmed false accepts are fixed-census counts (6/15, 21/23), not an independently sampled population rate; single author, no external replication yet
candidates.presentationReason: Method, fault grammar, and claim boundaries (mechanism vs. population rate) are stated precisely and repeatedly
candidates.reason: Directly audits two benchmarks widely used for agent leaderboards and verifier-reward RL training, with confirmed false-accept mechanisms backed by independent readback cross-validation rather than trusting the verifier's own output

candidates.title: Bookkeeping, Composition, or Unreachable Gold? Reading MemoryAgentBench's Conflict-Resolution Scores Against a Frozen Last-Write Resolver
candidates.venue: NeurIPS 2026 IAB Workshop (Interpreting Agent Behavior, non-archival)
candidates.citationVelocity: published 6 days (submitted 2026-10-06); Semantic Scholar API 429 rate-limited on every attempt, no data available
communitySignals: no independent Papers with Code entry found
credibilityEvidence: frozen zero-learning last-write resolver scores 80.25% official metric (74.5% on 3 held-out lists) with Clopper-Pearson intervals
67/items with released gold unreachable by the stated last-write rule, confirmed via documented reachability check (Appendix A)
inter-rater reliability check on 13 disputed labels, kappa=0.88
three systems' per-item accuracy stratified by reachability label (84.7/82.6/41.6% vs 10.4/11.9/6.0%)
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Covers only the benchmark's own 4 fact lists (800 items total); no learned/structured-memory system was run, only 2 long-context models + a BM25 agent reimplementation
reproducibilityEvidence: parser/resolver rules and labeling taxonomy documented in appendices with an internal hashed freeze timestamp record (not a third-party registry); no public code repo link found
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Statistical method (exact intervals, re-labeling reliability) and explicit scope limits (4 fact lists, no structured-memory system tested) match the claim strength used in the article
candidates.primaryLimitation: Covers only the benchmark's own 4 independent fact lists (all 800 items derive from these 4); conclusions about learned/structured memory systems are by analogy only, not direct evidence
candidates.presentationReason: Setup, freeze protocol, taxonomy, and limitations are documented precisely with pre-registration details
